passage: On the farm in Punjab, Gurpreet had a list in her head: wash hands, bring the plates, set out the water. Her daughter Madhuri, five, got lost after "wash hands" and stood by the tap, dripping. Gurpreet breathed out, knelt and said calmly, "Just the plates now." Madhuri carried them over. "Now the water jug," said Gurpreet, walking beside her. Madhuri smiled. "One by one."

qa.q: What did Gurpreet ask Madhuri to carry after washing hands?
qa.a: The plates.

qa.q: How might Madhuri have felt standing by the tap, dripping?
qa.a: Lost or unsure what to do next, since the list was long. She might also just have been enjoying the water.

qa.q: What made Gurpreet's second try work better?
qa.a: She gave one short step at a time in a calm voice and walked beside her.

qa.q: How might Gurpreet feel when Madhuri says "One by one"?
qa.a: Probably relieved and pleased that the calmer way worked.

grounding: Shows a preschooler following one-step instructions and getting lost in a long list, helped by calm repeated reminders.

passage: At the beach in Sydney, Alejandro said, "Freya, put on your hat, get the bucket, find your shoes, and don't run to the water." Freya, four, grabbed the bucket and ran towards the water. "Freya!" he said sharply. She stopped, her lip trembling. He walked over, crouched and held up her hat. "Hat first." She put it on. "Now the bucket." "Okay!" She lifted it and grinned.

qa.q: What did Freya grab first?
qa.a: The bucket.

qa.q: How did Freya probably feel when Alejandro spoke sharply?
qa.a: Hurt or startled, hinted by her trembling lip. She may also have been upset at having her game stopped.

qa.q: What could Alejandro do differently next time?
qa.a: Give one short instruction and show her, like holding up the hat, before adding the next step.

qa.q: How might Alejandro feel when Freya runs towards the water?
qa.a: He may be worried, since he says her name sharply, but he calms quickly and crouches to help her one step at a time.

grounding: Shows a preschooler failing a long instruction list and cooperating when shown one calm step at a time.

passage: In the KG classroom, Kamal Sir said, “Put your books in your bag, push in your chair, get your bottle, line up at the door and don't forget your caps.” Most children stood still, confused. Sabina picked up her bottle and sat down again. Kamal Sir laughed at himself. “Too much. One thing. Books in bags.” He showed them, sliding his book in. They copied. “Now chairs in.” He pushed his chair. Step by step, the class got ready. Sabina was first at the door.

qa.q: Where was Sabina at the end?
qa.a: First at the door.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling when she picked up her bottle and sat down again?
qa.a: She was probably confused by the long list and unsure what to do next.

qa.q: What went right once Kamal Sir changed his approach?
qa.a: He gave one step at a time and showed each one, which the children could follow.

qa.q: How might Kamal Sir see his first long instruction?
qa.a: He realised it was too much for them, and laughed at himself rather than blaming the children.

grounding: A teacher learns that short one-step instructions, shown as well as said, work better than a long list for preschoolers.

passage: I'm Usha, the neighbour who helps in the mornings. Hafsa's mother used to rush: “Shoes, bag, tiffin, hurry, why aren't you ready?” and Hafsa would sit on the floor. This week her mother tries something different. She says one thing: “Shoes.” She shows her own shoes. Hafsa puts hers on. Then: “Bag.” Hafsa picks it up. When she forgets, her mother just says, “Tiffin,” calmly, again. I don't know if Hafsa likes it better, but they leave on time now.

qa.q: What does Hafsa's mother say first?
qa.a: “Shoes.”

qa.q: What might Hafsa have been feeling when she sat on the floor in the rushed mornings?
qa.a: She was probably overwhelmed and upset by the long list and the scolding tone. Usha can't be sure, but she seems calmer now.

qa.q: What changed that helped the mornings?
qa.a: Her mother gave one short instruction at a time, showed it, and repeated reminders calmly.

qa.q: How does Usha see the new mornings?
qa.a: Usha notices that they leave on time now, though Usha isn't sure how Hafsa feels about it.

grounding: A neighbour observes a mother switch from rushed lists to calm one-step reminders that her preschooler follows.

passage:
Monday: “Sahil, brush your teeth, wear your uniform, comb your hair, why are you so slow?” Nazia snapped. Sahil stood in the corridor, not moving.
Wednesday: Nazia said calmly, “Teeth.” She brushed hers beside him. Then, “Uniform.” She held up his shirt. He put it on.
Friday: Nazia said, “Teeth,” and Sahil said, “I know! Then uniform!” He brushed, then got dressed. When he forgot his hair, she said, “Comb,” and he laughed and did it.

qa.q: What did Nazia hold up on Wednesday?
qa.a: His shirt.

qa.q: What was Sahil feeling when he stood in the corridor not moving on Monday?
qa.a: He was probably overwhelmed and upset by the long list and the snapping tone, so he froze.

qa.q: What small step helped Sahil most?
qa.a: Nazia gave one calm instruction at a time and showed him, like brushing her teeth beside him.

qa.q: How might Nazia feel on Friday when Sahil says “Then uniform!”?
qa.a: She is likely pleased and relieved that calm, repeated reminders are working.

grounding: Over a week, a mother learns that calm, one-step instructions and showing help her preschooler more than a scolded list.

passage:
The power had gone out and it was nearly bedtime. Madhuri lit a candle. "Kalyani, put your toys away, brush your teeth, find your nightie, and bring me your hairbrush."

Kalyani picked up one block and then sat and played with it.

"Kalyani! What did I just say?" Madhuri snapped.

Kalyani's lip wobbled. "I forgot."

Madhuri softened. "Sorry. Too many things at once. Just one: toys in the box. Watch." She dropped a block in. Kalyani copied her, block by block.

"Now: teeth," Madhuri said calmly. Kalyani ran for her toothbrush.

qa.q: What did Madhuri light when the power went out?
qa.a: A candle.

qa.q: What was Kalyani feeling when her lip wobbled and she said "I forgot"?
qa.a: She was most likely upset and a little ashamed at being snapped at, and probably overwhelmed by the long list. She may also have been tired at bedtime.

qa.q: What went wrong at first, and what fixed it?
qa.a: A long list and a scolding tone lost Kalyani; one calm step at a time, with Madhuri showing her, got the toys away and teeth started.

qa.q: How does Madhuri see the moment after she snaps?
qa.a: She realises she gave too many things at once, feels sorry, and changes to one clear step.

grounding: It shows a preschooler losing track of a long list but following calm, one-step instructions when also shown what to do.
